title: Your first task with the Claude desktop app

steps.title: What we'll do today
steps.html:
You'll install the Claude desktop app and give Claude Code, inside it, its first job. No black text window: you use it by clicking buttons.

  • Time: 20–30 minutes
  • You need: a computer (Windows or Mac), internet, and a payment card for a paid plan
Tip — Open this page on your phone and follow along on your computer. On your phone, just go to: earlln.com/lab.html

Don't worry about unfamiliar words. We explain each one the first time it comes up.

faq.a: An AI assistant you give jobs to in plain words. Ask it something like "tidy up this file" and it creates and edits files for you.
Yes. Claude Code needs a paid Claude plan (Pro or higher) billed monthly. You'll see the exact price when you sign up. A free account can't use it.
This practice needs a computer. Phone and tablet practices are coming soon.

steps.title: Which computer will you install Claude Code on?
steps.html: Pick the computer you'll install it on, not necessarily the device you're reading this on.

choices.label: I'm not sure
choices.sub: We'll show you how to check

steps.title: How to tell Windows from Mac
steps.html:
Look at the computer's keyboard.

  • A ⊞ (window) key at the bottom left → Windows
  • A ⌘ command key → Mac

An apple logo on the back or lid also means it's a Mac.
steps.button: Got it, let me choose again

steps.title: This practice needs a computer
steps.html:
Claude Code is a program you install on a computer. Practices for phones and tablets are coming soon.

Come back when you have a home or work computer. Your progress is saved in this browser.

steps.title: Do you have a Claude account?
steps.html: Claude Code needs a paid Claude account (Pro or higher).

choices.label: I only have a free account

steps.title: Sign up for Claude
steps.html:
First, open a browser on your computer. A browser is the program you use to look at the internet. Click one of these icons at the bottom of your screen:

  • Windows: Microsoft Edge (blue wave) or Chrome (red, yellow and green circle)
  • Mac: Safari (compass) or Chrome
  1. Click the address bar at the very top of the browser, type claude.ai and press Enter.
  2. Choose Continue with Google, or sign up with your email address.
  3. If you used email, open the confirmation email in your inbox and click its button.

check.q: Did you finish signing up and see the Claude chat screen?

faq.a: It's the long box at the very top of the browser where you can type. It usually shows an address starting with https://. Click it once and the text turns blue; then just type claude.ai.
It's the big key on the right side of the keyboard, marked Enter or ↵. On a Mac it may say return.

steps.title: If signing up doesn't work
steps.html:
• If the confirmation email doesn't arrive, check your spam folder.
  • If you have a Google account, Continue with Google is the easiest.
  • If it asks for your country, pick the one you live in.

steps.title: Subscribe to a paid plan (Pro)
steps.html:
1. On claude.ai, find and click the Upgrade button or menu.
  2. Choose the Pro plan. (Max also works, but Pro is plenty to start.)
  3. Enter your card details and pay.
Check the payment yourself — read the price and whether it renews every month before you continue. You can cancel any time.

check.noLabel: I can't find the Upgrade button

steps.title: Finding the Upgrade menu
steps.html:
The screen layout changes from time to time. Check these places:

  • The menu that opens when you click your name (or your initial in a circle) at the bottom left
  • The word Upgrade near the top or near the chat box

Still can't find it? Ask Claude in the chat box: "Where do I upgrade my plan?" It will tell you.

steps.title: How to tell if your account is paid
steps.html:
Go to claude.ai in your browser.

  • If you see a sign-in screen → sign in if you have an account, or choose I don't have an account.
  • If you see Pro or Max near your name at the bottom left → it's paid.
  • If an Upgrade button stands out → it's probably free.
steps.button: Got it, let me choose again

steps.title: Get a Claude window ready for your questions
steps.html:
If you get stuck during the practice, you can ask Claude directly. Let's try it once now.

  1. Tap I have a question below to open it.
  2. Type What is Claude Code? and press Ask Claude.
  3. A new window (or the Claude app) opens. Check the chat box:
    · If your question is already there → press Enter
    · If it's empty → click the box once, paste, then press Enter
What is pasting? — It puts in the text you copied. On a computer press {{paste}} together; on a phone, press and hold the box, then tap Paste.

When you've seen the answer, come back here. You can ask like this any time you get stuck.

steps.title: If asking Claude doesn't work
steps.html:
• If no new window opens, go to claude.ai in your browser and type your question in the chat box. It's the same thing.
  • If you see a sign-in screen, sign in with your account.
  • This step is just practice, so it's fine to move on even if it doesn't work.

choices.label: Skip for now
choices.sub: I'll ask on claude.ai if I get stuck

steps.title: Name your practice folder
steps.html:
Claude Code works inside one folder that you choose. To start, it's safest to practice in an empty folder.

Choose a folder name. If you're not sure, just keep Practice.

steps.title: Make a '{{folder}}' folder on your desktop

win.html:
The desktop is the background screen you see when the computer starts. If windows are open, click — (minimize) at their top right to tuck them away.

  1. Put your mouse on an empty spot of the desktop and click the right mouse button.
  2. In the menu, click New → Folder.
  3. When the name box turns blue, type {{folder}} and press Enter.

mac.html:
The desktop is the background screen you see when the computer starts.

  1. Right-click an empty spot on the desktop.
    On a Mac trackpad, press with two fingers together to right-click.
  2. Click New Folder in the menu.
  3. While the new folder's name (untitled folder) is selected, type {{folder}} and press return.

check.q: Is there a '{{folder}}' folder on your desktop now?

faq.a: Click the folder once, then press <kbd>F2</kbd> on Windows or <kbd>return</kbd> on a Mac to type the name again.

steps.title: If making the folder doesn't work

win.html:
• If you don't see New in the menu, right-click a completely empty spot, not on an icon.
  • If you can't see the desktop, press ⊞+D together to tuck all windows away.

mac.html:
• If no menu appears, hold the control key and click the desktop. That's also a right-click.
  • Or click the desktop once, then choose File → New Folder from the menu at the very top of the screen.

steps.title: Download the Claude desktop app
steps.html:
1. Open a web browser on your computer.
  2. Click the address bar at the top, type claude.ai/download and press Enter.
  3. Click the button for your computer: Download for Windows or Download for macOS.
steps.alt: Clicking the download button for your computer

steps.title: If the download doesn't work
steps.html:
• Check you typed the address exactly: claude.ai/download.
  • If nothing seems to happen, look for a download indicator at the top (or bottom) of the browser.
  • Work computers may block installing programs. In that case, ask your IT team.

win.html:
1. Click the downloaded file, or double-click the Claude installer in your Downloads folder.
  2. If it asks "Do you want to allow this app to make changes to your device?", click Yes.
  3. When it's installed, the Claude app opens by itself.

mac.html:
1. Double-click the Claude file (.dmg) in your Downloads folder.
  2. In the window that opens, drag the Claude icon onto the Applications folder.
  3. In Finder, go to Applications and double-click Claude. If it warns the app was downloaded from the internet, click Open.

win.html:
• The Downloads folder is in the list on the left of File Explorer (the yellow folder icon).
  • If a blue warning like "Windows protected your PC" appears, check the file came from claude.ai before continuing.
  • Work computers may block installs. Ask your IT team.

mac.html:
• Make sure you dragged the icon in the .dmg window. That's what puts it into Applications.
  • If you see a warning about an unidentified developer, check the file came from claude.ai and click Open.

steps.title: Sign in to the app
steps.html:
When the app opens, you'll see a sign-in screen. Sign in with the account you subscribed with (Pro or higher).

  • Continue with Google, or sign in with your email address
  • If a browser opens asking you to confirm, sign in, approve, and come back to the app.

check.q: Are you signed in and can you see the app?

steps.title: If signing in doesn't work
steps.html:
• Use the same account you signed up and subscribed with. (If you used Google, use Google.)
  • With email, you need to enter the link or code from the confirmation email. Check your spam folder too.

steps.title: Open the Code tab
steps.html:
At the top left of the app there are tabs such as Chat · Cowork · Code. Click Code.

Code is Claude Code. Here, Claude can create and edit files on your computer directly. (Chat is the conversation screen you tried in Practice 0.)
steps.alt: Clicking the Code tab at the top left of the app

check.q: Did the Code screen (with a typing box at the bottom) appear?

steps.title: If you can't see the Code tab
steps.html:
• Check you signed in with a paid (Pro or higher) account. Free accounts can't use Code.
  • Update the app to the latest version and open it again.
  • If the window is very narrow the tabs can be hidden. Make the window bigger.

steps.title: Choose the folder to work in (1)
steps.html:
Claude Code works only inside the folder you choose. So choose the '{{folder}}' folder.

  1. Check that the first button under the typing box says Local (your computer). If not, click it and choose Local.
  2. Click the folder button next to it, then Open folder… in the list.
steps.alt: Checking Local and choosing Open folder from the folder button

steps.title: Choose the folder to work in (2)

win.html:
1. In the folder window, click Desktop on the left.
  2. Click the {{folder}} folder once. (Double-clicking opens it, which is fine too.)
  3. Click Select Folder at the bottom.

mac.html:
1. In the folder window, click Desktop on the left.
  2. Click the {{folder}} folder once.
  3. Click Open at the bottom.

steps.alt: Choosing the Practice folder in the folder window

check.q: Does the folder button under the typing box now show '{{folder}}'?

steps.title: If choosing the folder doesn't work
steps.html:
• If you can't see the desktop in the window, scroll the list on the left to find Desktop.
  • If you went inside the folder, you can click Select Folder (Open on a Mac) from there.
  • If you chose the wrong folder, click the folder button again and start from Open folder….

steps.title: Check the permission mode — Manual
steps.html:
Look at the button on the right under the typing box. It should say Manual.

Manual means Claude asks you every time before creating or editing a file. Keep it on Manual to start.

If you see another name (Accept edits, Auto, etc.), click it and choose Manual. You'll learn the other modes later.

steps.title: Give it a first task
steps.html: Now give Claude a job in plain words. Paste or type the sentence below into the box and press Enter (return on a Mac).
steps.code: Create a file called todo.txt and write 3 example to-dos for today

steps.title: "May I create it?" — give permission
steps.html:
Claude always asks first before creating a file. A card shows what it will create; the green lines are what will be added.

Check it and click Allow (usually blue).

The button may be labeled differently (Allow, Accept…). Click the one that gives permission.
steps.alt: Clicking Allow on the permission card before the file is created

steps.title: If no permission card appears
steps.html:
• Claude may still be thinking. Wait a few seconds.
  • If it already says it created the file, the mode may not be Manual. Go on and check the file, and switch the mode to Manual.
  • If Claude asks something back, type your answer and press Enter.

steps.title: See the result with your own eyes
steps.html: Double-click the {{folder}} folder on your desktop. todo.txt is there. Double-click it to see the to-dos Claude wrote.
steps.alt: todo.txt has appeared in the folder

check.q: Do you see todo.txt in the '{{folder}}' folder?

steps.title: If you can't see the file
steps.html:
• Check that the folder button under the typing box shows {{folder}}. If it was another folder, the file may be there.
  • Ask Claude, "Where did you create todo.txt?"
  • Closing and reopening the folder window sometimes helps.

steps.title: Finishing up
steps.html:
That's it for today. Just close the app.

Today's conversation stays in the list on the left. Next time, open the app, go to the Code tab and click it to carry on. You don't need to install or sign in again.

steps.title: 🎉 First practice done! What you learned
steps.html:
You made it all the way. Here's a short recap.

Youask in wordsClaude Codewith permissionFile done

New words

Desktop appThe Claude program you install on your computer. It has Chat, Code and more inside
Code tabWhere Claude works on your files directly. This is Claude Code
Local · folderButtons to choose which folder on your computer (Local) it works in
ManualThe permission mode that asks every time before creating or editing

Two things to remember

  1. Claude Code works only inside the folder you choose. Choose the folder first.
  2. It always asks before creating or changing anything. Things only change when you read the card and click Allow.

Next step

In the next practice you'll have it edit today's todo.txt and learn to read the changes (red and green lines).
